questions.text: Consider clock timing. A. Insertion delay needs a defined source and sink. B. Equal insertion delays at two sinks imply zero pairwise skew under the same reference. C. Every sink's insertion delay equals the data-path cycle count. Which statements are correct?
Define skew as capture arrival minus launch arrival. Clock arrivals are 0.55 ns at capture and 0.35 ns at launch. What is skew?
Two sinks each have clock insertion delay 1 ns relative to the same reference. What is their pairwise skew?

Consider physical clock buffering. A. Sink capacitance loads the clock network. B. Wires affect clock delay and slew. C. Correct logical toggling proves ideal physical delivery. Which statements are correct?
Consider CTS objectives. A. Skew and insertion delay can matter. B. Slew, loading and power can matter. C. A CTS pass alone proves the product algorithm correct. Which statements are correct?
Why may a geometrically symmetric H-tree still have nonzero electrical skew?
options: Loads, parasitics, cell variation and routing details can differ.
Geometric symmetry guarantees identical electrical conditions in every real design.
Electrical skew depends only on the number of RTL comments.

questions.text: What is one trade-off of a clock mesh compared with a simple tree?
options: Potentially robust clock delivery at the cost of substantial wiring and switching load.
Guaranteed absence of any routing demand.

questions.text: What does useful skew attempt to exploit?
options: Replace every data path with a clock wire.
Remove all hold checks from signoff.
Intentional relative clock timing to improve selected timing margins with other checks preserved.

questions.text: With capture-minus-launch skew convention, positive useful skew can have what trade-off?
options: Better setup margin but reduced hold margin.
Worse setup and better hold margin always.
Better setup and hold margin by the same amount always.

questions.text: Nominal setup slack is 60 ps at zero skew. Capture arrives 30 ps later relative to launch, with other quantities fixed. New setup slack is what?
Nominal hold slack is 30 ps at zero skew. Capture arrives 30 ps later relative to launch, with other quantities fixed. New hold slack is what?
Setup slack at zero skew is 60 ps and hold slack is 30 ps. With k=capture-minus-launch and other values fixed, which skew interval satisfies both ideal checks?
options: Any positive skew without a bound.

questions.text: Why should clock gating cells and their enables receive timing checks?
options: Clock-gating timing applies only to source-code compilation.
The gating operation must avoid unsafe clock pulses and respect control timing.
Gated clocks can never glitch under any enable transition.
Gating eliminates the need for clock distribution.

questions.text: What is a clock-tree sink?
options: Every signal port regardless of use.
A destination clock pin or specified endpoint of the clock network.

questions.text: Source latency is 2.0 ns and modeled network latency is 0.6 ns. What is their total under an additive convention?
What does global routing primarily produce?
options: A coarse routing plan allocating paths and resources.
Every final legal wire polygon and via in all cases.

questions.text: What does detailed routing add beyond global routing?
options: Only an ideal zero-resistance connectivity graph.
Exact tracks, layers, wire segments and vias subject to detailed rules.
Only a list of function names.

questions.text: When does routing overflow occur on a resource?
options: The netlist has more than one module.

questions.text: An edge has capacity 8 tracks and demand 11 tracks. What is its overflow?
Two routing edges have (demand,capacity)=(7,5) and (6,8). Sum positive overflow on the edges.
What does zero global-routing overflow establish by itself?
options: Every detailed design rule necessarily passes.
The coarse capacity model has no overflow, but detailed legality still needs checking.
No vias are needed in the design.

questions.text: Why can a global route require a detour?
options: Obstacles or congested resources can prevent the shortest coarse path.
Every routed net must be a straight Euclidean line.

questions.text: For rectilinear routing with no obstacles, what is the Manhattan distance from (3,5) to (10,1)?
What is the role of a via in multilayer routing?
options: Connect conductors across selected metal layers.
Set every sink's data value to zero.
Replace the need for a timing library.

questions.text: Why can redundant vias improve reliability?
options: They remove every need for physical rules.
They change an AND function into an OR function.
They guarantee no routing area cost.
Multiple valid connections can reduce dependence on one via and may lower resistance.

questions.text: What must redundant-via insertion respect?
options: Applicable geometry, spacing and connectivity constraints.

questions.text: What does a routing DRC violation indicate?
options: The Boolean function is necessarily wrong on every input.
A geometric implementation condition fails a specified design rule.
The source-code file cannot be parsed.

questions.text: Why are minimum spacing rules needed?
options: To meet process-dependent manufacturability and electrical separation requirements.
To guarantee equal delays on all nets.
To create unknown values in simulation.
To force all connected pins apart logically.

questions.text: What is a routing rip-up-and-reroute step?
options: Remove selected route segments and try an alternative implementation.
Dismiss every DRC without fixing it.

questions.text: Why can routing-order choices affect congestion?
options: Every net has its own unlimited private routing layer.
Earlier nets can occupy resources needed by later nets.
Net order determines the truth table directly.

questions.text: What does parasitic extraction derive?
options: The minimum Boolean cover from a clock waveform alone.
The original software source from a package label.
Electrical resistance and capacitance associated with physical interconnect.

questions.text: What is a common use of SPEF in implementation analysis?
Why is post-route extraction useful for timing?
options: Actual wire geometry can yield more realistic RC than early estimates.
It removes every cell timing arc.

questions.text: Under a simple uniform-wire model, R scales with length. If length increases 50% with cross-section unchanged, resistance scales by what?
A driver sees 6 fF of pin load and 9 fF of wire capacitance. Ignoring coupling, total load is what?
For a two-section RC tree with ground capacitances C1 at the first node and C2 at the sink, which Elmore expression applies at the sink, ignoring driver resistance?
Using that two-section model, R1=2 kilohms, R2=1 kilohm, C1=3 fF and C2=5 fF. What is the Elmore time constant?
Why can coupling capacitance require more context than a fixed ground capacitance?
options: Its effect can depend on neighboring-net transitions.
It is determined only by RTL variable names.
It always cancels wire resistance completely.
It has no possible effect on delay or noise.

questions.text: What does LVS verify after routing?
options: Extracted layout connectivity matches the intended reference within the check's scope.
Every path meets setup and hold.

questions.text: Why does a DRC-clean result not establish timing closure?
options: DRC always computes every clock-domain property.
Timing depends only on geometry-rule count.
Geometry rules and timing requirements are different checks.
A legal wire has exactly zero delay.

questions.text: What does tapeout release for manufacture?
options: Final approved design data, commonly including a GDSII or equivalent layout database.

questions.text: What is a GDSII stream primarily used to represent?
options: Geometric layout data with hierarchy and layers.

questions.text: Why should final signoff use the final routed design version?
options: Version identity affects only file naming.
Old analysis always proves every future change.
Every route change is electrically identical by definition.
Late ECOs and route changes can invalidate earlier analysis results.

questions.text: A post-route hold path has slack -12 ps. A proposed data buffer adds at least 20 ps delay without other changes. What is its new ideal hold slack?
A setup path has slack 18 ps. Its reroute adds 25 ps maximum delay. All else fixed, new setup slack is what?
Why should setup and hold both be rechecked after a clock-tree ECO?
options: Clock changes affect only source-code compilation.
Clock sinks are independent of timing constraints.
A setup pass necessarily proves hold.
Relative launch/capture clock changes can affect the checks in opposite directions.

questions.text: Consider a late buffer ECO. A. Added cells need legal physical locations. B. New connections can affect DRC and timing. C. Previous signoff automatically remains valid without reanalysis. Which statements are correct?

Consider antenna cleanup. A. Current routing must meet applicable process antenna rules. B. A layer jump or diode may be a valid remedy in the appropriate flow. C. Timing closure alone proves all antenna checks pass. Which statements are correct?
What is the purpose of maintaining final constraint and parasitic provenance?
options: Replace all numerical analysis with file names.
Guarantee every source file was written by one person.
Ensure signoff results correspond to the intended clocks, exceptions and physical network.
Remove the need for design review.

questions.text: Which statement best describes signoff readiness?
options: No extracted interconnect is ever needed after routing.
Required functional, timing, electrical and physical checks pass for the intended design version and scenarios.
A clean source-code compile guarantees manufacture-ready layout.
One favorable setup report is sufficient for every requirement.
